chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Ahmad al-Sa'igh (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hamdani narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) led his companions in the Fajr prayer one day. Then he sat with them conversing until the sun rose. One man after another began to rise and leave until only two men remained with him: an Ansari and a Thaqafi. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to them: "I know that you two have a need and wish to ask me about it. If you wish, I shall inform you of your need before you ask me; and if you wish, ask me." They said: "Rather, you inform us, O Messenger of God, for that would be clearer for the blind, further from doubt, and more steadfast for faith." So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: "As for you, O brother of the Ansar, you are from a people who prefer others over themselves. You are a villager and this Thaqafi is a Bedouin — do you defer to him in asking?" He said: "Yes."

So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: "As for you, O brother of Thaqif, you came to ask me about your wudu and your salat and what reward you have in them. Know that when you plunge your hand in the water and say: 'In the name of God' (bismillah), the sins acquired by your hands will scatter. When you wash your face, the sins acquired by your eyes through their gaze and by your mouth through its speech will scatter. When you wash your arms, the sins to your right and your left will scatter. When you wipe your head and feet, the sins that your feet walked toward will scatter. This is for you in your wudu. When you stand for prayer, face the qibla, recite the Mother of the Book (al-Fatiha) and whatever is easy for you from the chapters, then bow and complete the bowing and prostration, testify the shahada, and recite the taslim — every sin between the previous prayer and the next prayer will be forgiven for you. This is for you in your prayer."

"As for you, O brother of the Ansar, you came to ask me about your Hajj and your 'Umra and what reward you have in them. Know that when you set out on the path of Hajj and mount your riding beast, and your riding beast carries you — every time your beast sets its hoof down and lifts it up, God will record a good deed for you and erase a sin from you. When you enter ihram and recite the talbiyya, God will record ten good deeds for you and erase ten sins from you for every talbiyya. When you circumambulate the House seven times (tawaf), you will have thereby a covenant with God, Mighty and Majestic, and a mention, such that your Lord would be too ashamed to punish you after it. When you pray two rak'as at the Maqam (Ibrahim), God will record two thousand accepted rak'as for you. When you perform the sa'i between al-Safa and al-Marwa seven times, you will have thereby with God, Mighty and Majestic, a reward like one who made Hajj walking from his hometown, and a reward like one who freed seventy believing souls. When you stand at 'Arafat until sunset, even if you had sins equivalent to the grains of sand in 'Alij and the foam of the sea, God would forgive them all for you. When you pelt the jamarat (pillars), God will record ten good deeds for every pebble, to be recorded for you for the remainder of your life. When you slaughter your sacrificial animal or sacrifice your camel, God will record a good deed for every drop of its blood, to be recorded for you for the remainder of your life. When you circumambulate the House seven times for the visitation (tawaf al-ziyara) and pray two rak'as at the Maqam, a noble angel will strike your shoulders and then say: 'As for what has passed, it has been forgiven for you — so begin anew your deeds for the time between now and one hundred and twenty days.'"

key_terms.أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ: The Mother of the Book — Surat al-Fatiha, the opening chapter of the Quran, recited in every prayer
key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةُ: Talbiyya — the Hajj invocation 'Labbayk Allahumma labbayk' (Here I am, O God, here I am)
key_terms.الثَّوَابُ: Reward — spiritual merit earned through acts of worship
key_terms.تَنَاثَرَتِ الذُّنُوبُ: The sins scatter/fall away — a vivid image of purification during wudu
key_terms.تَوَافُ الزِّيَارَةِ: Tawaf al-ziyara — the obligatory circumambulation after 'Arafat, one of the pillars of Hajj
key_terms.رَمْلُ عَالِجٍ: 'Alij sand — a vast desert region in Arabia, used hyperbolically to signify an immense quantity of sins

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards of wudu, prayer, Hajj and 'Umra according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted by Imam al-Baqir (AS) from the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), presents a remarkable scene from Medina in which the Prophet, after the Fajr prayer, privately addresses two remaining companions — one from the Ansar and one from Thaqif — regarding the spiritual rewards of their religious practices. The Thaqafi is taught the purifying effects of wudu (ablution) step by step, and the comprehensive forgiveness offered by each salat (prayer). The Ansari is then taught the immense rewards of every act of Hajj and 'Umra — from the first step of the journey to the final tawaf — culminating in the promise of total forgiveness and a fresh start lasting 120 days. This teaching underscores the transformative spiritual power of worship in the Shia tradition, portraying ablution, prayer, and pilgrimage not merely as ritual obligations but as comprehensive mechanisms for purification of the soul.
word_analysis: al-Baqir (the one who splits open knowledge)
